'''Edrice Adebayo''' (born July 18, 1997), nicknamed '''Bam''', is an American [[basketball]] player. He played one season of college basketball for the [[University of Kentucky]]. Adebayo became a five-star recruit and considered one of the best players in the Class of 2016 by most recruiting services.

==Early life==
Adebayo got the nickname “Bam Bam” (after [[Bamm-Bamm]] Rubble) from his aunt after he picked up a coffee table while watching ''[[The Flintstones]]'' when he was just 1.<ref name=BAMcommit2>{{cite web|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2015/five-star-forward-edrice-bam-adebayo-picks-kentuckyn-c-state-bam-adebayo-high-point-christian|title=Five-star forward Edrice 'Bam' Adebayo picks Kentucky|accessdate=2015-11-17|date=2015-11-17|publisher=[[USA Today]]|author=Jordan, Jason}}</ref> He subsequently moved to North Carolina.

==High school career== 
[[File: 20160330 MCDAAG Bam Adebayo on  defense.jpg|190px|thumb|Right|Adebayo blocks the ball  at the [[2016 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]]] 
His junior year he attended [[Northside High School (Pinetown, North Carolina)|Northside High School]] in [[Pinetown, North Carolina]], where he averaged 32.2 points and 21 rebounds per game. During the spring and summer of 2015, Adebayo competed on the [[Adidas]] Uprising Gauntlet Circuit for the  [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) team, Team Loaded North Carolina (NC) where he played alongside fellow five-star recruit [[Dennis Smith Jr.]]. He averaged 14.2 [[points per game]] and 10.2 [[rebounds per game]] on the Adidas Uprising Gauntlet Circuit. Adebayo participated in the NBPA Top 100 camp on June 22, 2015 at the [[John Paul Jones Arena]] in [[Charlottesville, Virginia|Virginia]], and the Adidas Nations camp. In August of 2015, Adebayo was selected to play in the [[Under Armour]] Elite 24 invitational in [[Brooklyn, New York]], where he outshined the competition scoring 21 points and 8 rebounds leading the East to a 111-110 victory over the West team, and earned Elite 24 MVP honors  alongside [[Josh Jackson (basketball)|Josh Jackson]] and [[Frank Jackson (basketball)|Frank Jackson]]. <ref name="BAMcommit2" /> After his junior season he transferred to [[High Point Christian Academy]] in [[High Point, North Carolina]]. <ref>{{cite web|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2015/hoops-star-edrice-bam-adebayo-reportedly-to-transfer-to-high-point-christian-for-senior-year|title=Hoops star Edrice 'Bam' Adebayo to transfer to High Point Christian for senior year|accessdate=2015-11-17|date=2015-08-15|publisher=[[USA Today]]|author=Jordan, Jason}}</ref> In his senior season at HPCA, Adebayo averaged 18.9 [[points per game]], 13.0 [[rebounds per game]], 1.4 blocks per game and 1.5 assist per game. Adebayo led the Cougars to a NCISAA state championship appearance, where they lost 67-53 to [[Providence Day School]]. <ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/high-school/article61588947.html}}</ref>  He was named [[North Carolina Mr. Basketball]] in 2016. In January 2016, Adebayo was named a [[McDonald's All-American]] and  played in the [[2016 McDonald's All-American Game]] on March 30th, at the [[United Center]] in Chicago, IL, where he scored 16 points and 12 rebounds in a 114-107 loss to the West team. Adebayo also competed in the 2016 [[Jordan Brand Classic]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.usatodayhss.com/2016/edrice-adebayos-hard-work-earned-him-his-mcdonalds-all-american-jersey|title=Edrice Adebayo's hard work earned him his McDonald's All American Jersey|last=Jordan|first=Jason|date=February 12, 2016|work=Www.usatodayhss.com|access-date=April 6, 2017|archive-url=|archive-date=|dead-url=}}</ref> Adebayo was rated as a five-star recruit and ranked the No. 5 overall player to in the 2016 high school class by [[ESPN]], while [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] ranked him No. 6 in the 2016 class. 
He committed to Kentucky on November 17, live on ESPN's [[Mike and Mike in the morning|Mike & Mike]] simulcast radio show.<ref name=BAMcommit>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/recruiting/basketball/story/_/id/14152175/edrice-bam-adebayo-commits-kentucky-wildcats|title=No. 6 recruit Edrice 'Bam' Adebayo commits to Kentucky|accessdate=2015-11-17|date=2015-11-17|publisher=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref> He chose Kentucky over [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]] and [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]].

He’s ranked in the top 10 by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] (No. 6) and [[ESPNU Recruiting Insider|ESPN]] (No. 6). 247Sports (No. 14) and [[Scout.com|Scout]] (No. 15) tab him as a top-15 prospect in the 2016 class. He has prior USA Basketball experience and was named a [[MaxPreps.com|MaxPreps]] All-American in 2013.<ref name=Fallsignees>{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/news/kentucky-men-s-basketball-signs-six-in-fall-signing-11-19-2015|title=Kentucky Men’s Basketball Signs Six in Fall Signing Period|accessdate=2015-11-19|date=2014-11-19|publisher=University of Kentucky}}</ref>

==College career ==  
[[File:Bam-Adebayo-2.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Adebayo in Kentucky's 2016 Blue-White scrimmage]]
On November 17, 2015, Adebayo Committed to the University Of Kentucky. He joined fellow freshmen [[Malik Monk]], [[De'Aaron Fox]], and [[Wenyen Gabriel]]. On December 7, 2016, Adebayo recorded 16 points and 7 rebounds in a 87-67 win against the  [[Valparaiso Crusaders]]. On February 21, 2017, Adebayo scored 22 points and 15 rebounds to defeat the [[Missouri Tigers]] in a 72-62 Victory.  As the number one seed entering the [[2017 SEC Men's Basketball Tournament|SEC Tournament]], Kentucky would defeat the [[Georgia Bulldogs]] in the quarterfinals and beat Alabama in the semi-finals. On March 12, 2017, Adebayo grabbed 9 rebounds to help the Wildcats defeat Arkansas 82-65 and win the SEC Championship. On March 17, 2017, in the first round of the [[2017 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]], Adebayo had 18 rebounds in a 79-70 Victory against [[Northern Kentucky University]]. In the second round of the NCAA Tournament, Adebayo secured 10 rebounds to help Kentucky defeat [[Wichita State University]]. On March 24, 2017, Kentucky defeated the [[UCLA Bruins]] in the Sweet sixteen, Adebayo had 12 rebounds in the game. On March 26, 2017, Adebayo scored 13 points and 7 rebounds in a 75-73 loss in the Elite eight against the [[North Carolina Tar Heels]]. After losing in the Elite Eight in a heartbreaking fashion, he declared his entry into the [[2017 NBA draft]] on April 5, 2017, with him signing an agent twenty days later.<ref>http://www.bleacherreport.com/articles/2705653-bam-adebayo-signs-with-agent-will-officially-leave-kentucky-for-2017-nba-draft</ref> In 38 games for Kentucky in 2016-17, Adebayo averaged 13.0 points, 12.0 rebounds, and 1.5 blocks per game.
